sentences.text:
THIS MFA IS FILED UNDER SECTION 173(1) OF THE MOTOR VEHICLES ACT, 1988 PRAYING TO SET ASIDE THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 15.12.2014 PASSED IN MVC NO.1086/2012 ON THE FILE OF THE COURT OF PRINCIPAL SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS TRIBUNAL NO.V AT VIJAYPUR AND ALLOW THIS APPEAL BY ENHANCING THE COMPENSATION AMOUNT BY RS.10,00,000/-
ONLY AS CLAIMED BY THE APPELLANT.

THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT 1.

The claimant is in appeal challenging the correctness of the dismissal the claim petition by the Principal Senior Civil Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal No.V at Vijaypur in MVC No.1086/2012 vide Judgment and Award dated 15.12.2014.
2.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal No.V at Vijaypur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The claim petition discloses that on 19.04.2012 at about 10.00 p.m., when the claimant was riding pillion on a motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-24/J-4481, the rider lost control due to his rash and negligent riding.

As a result, the claimant fell down and suffered injuries to his left leg, left knee,
left palm and other injuries.
He was shifted to District Hospital, Vijayapura for treatment where he was treated as an inpatient and thereafter, he was NC: 2023:KHC-K:1137 shifted to a private hospital at Bijapur.

The claimant contended that the injuries were due to the rash and negligent riding by the rider of the motorcycle and he therefore, filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- from the owner & insurer of the motorcycle.
3. The owner of the motorcycle denied the age, income, occupation and nature of the injuries suffered by the claimant and denied the manner in which the accident had happened.
He claimed that he had sold the motorcycle and that it was insured at the relevant point of time.
4. The insurer contested the claim petition and denied the age, occupation and injury suffered by the claimant.
It also denied the accident.
It contended that the motorcycle was ridden by a person named Hameedsaheb Patel.

It claimed that the said Hameed NC: 2023:KHC-K:1137 Saheb Patel did not have a valid and effective driving licence and the owner of the motorcycle had entrusted it to an unauthorized person and it was therefore not liable to pay the compensation.
5. Based on these rival contentions, the claim petition was set down for trial.
The claimant was examined as PW.1 and he marked Ex.P1 to P6.

The subsequent transferee of the motorcycle was examined as RW.1 and one of the officials of the insurer was examined as RW.2 and Exs.R1 to R3 Ashok S/O Pandu Rathod vs Basavaraj S/O Sharanappa Jeer on 15 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92946760/
2 were marked.
6. Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal held that the claimant was proceeding on the offending motorcycle, which was ridden by a person named Abid Saheb Patel as per the FIR which was based on a complaint by the brother of the claimant.

entities.text: Ashok S/O Pandu Rathod vs Basavaraj S/O Sharanappa Jeer
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, the police had filed a charge sheet against a person named Hameed Saheb Patel.
It noticed that PW.1 had deposed that the motorcycle was ridden by Abid Saheb Patel.
It held of Abid Saheb Patel did not have a licence to ride the NC: 2023:KHC-K:1137 offending motorcycle.
It also noticed that Ex.R2 was the driving licence of Hameed Saheb Patel and held that he was not related to the person named Abid Saheb Patel.
It also held the jurisdictional police had charge sheeted a person named Hameed Saheb Patel and not Abid Saheb Patel only to sustain a claim for compensation.

Taking into account these facts,
the Tribunal held that the offending motorcycle was ridden by a person named Abid Saheb Patel,
who did not possess a licence as on the date of the accident.
Consequently, the claim petition filed by the claimant was dismissed.
7. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment, the claimant is before this Court.

8. The learned counsel for the appellant/claimant submitted that the name of the rider of the offending motorcycle was indeed mentioned as Abid Saheb Patel by the brother of the claimant instead of Hameed Saheb Patel.
He contended that the brother of the claimant was not aware of the correct name of the rider.

He contended NC: 2023:KHC-K:1137 that the name of rider was Hameed Saheb Patel and the same is evident from his driving licence at Ex.R2.
9.
Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent/insurer contended that the rider of the offending motorcycle was none other than the friend of the brother of the claimant.
He submits that the brother of the claimant himself mentioned the name of the rider of the offending motorcycle as Hameed Saheb Patel and not Abid Saheb Patel.
He therefore contends that Hameed Saheb Patel and Abid Saheb Patel are different persons.
He further submits that the claimant did not examine the said Hameed Saheb Patel before the Court and therefore there is a doubt about involvement of Abid Saheb Patil.
He further submits that the case sheet maintained at District Hospital at Vijayapur indicated that the claimant was drunk.

He contends that the offending motorcycle was ridden by the claimant himself and due to his intoxication, he lost control over the motorcycle and fell down and now NC: 2023:KHC-K:1137 a stranger was set up to lay a false claim against the insurer.
10. I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the appellant/claimant and learned counsel for the respondent/insurer.
11. The accident in question happened on 19.04.2012 at 10.00 p.m.

The injured was shifted to the District Hospital at Vijayapur and the wound certificate indicates that the claimant had suffered injuries due to fall from the motorcycle at Banjara cross about 9.30 p.m. on 19.04.2012 and he was accompanied by a friend namely, Valu Naik.
It also discloses that the claimant was emanating smell of alcohol from the mouth.

However, a complaint was lodged by the brother of the claimant on 22.04.2012, wherein, he claimed that the claimant and his friend named Abid Saheb Patel were riding the motorcycle on 19.04.2012 and that the rider Abid Saheb Patil dashed against a road Ashok S/O Pandu Rathod vs Basavaraj S/O Sharanappa Jeer on 15 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92946760/
3 divider.

The person named Abid Saheb Patel was a friend of the brother of the claimant and NC:
2023:KHC-K:1137 therefore, there cannot be any doubt that Abid Saheb Patel was riding the motorcycle at the time of the accident.
However, the claimant did not examine the said Abid Sabheb Patel.
He also did not produce any driving licence of the said Abid Saheb Patel.
He also did not examine his brother.
However, the jurisdictional police after investigating the crime filed a charge sheet against Hameed Saheb Patel, who allegedly was the rider of the offending motorcycle.
Therefore, the case of the claimant is hazy and gives an impression that the person named Hameed Saheb Patel was implicated in the case to make a wrongful gain.
However, it could also be possible that Hameed Saheb Patel was wrongly referred as 'Abid Saheb Patel'.
There is also no clear indication as to whether the claimant was riding the offending motorcycle as on the date of the accident.
There is also no clear indication that he was fully drunk and was not in a position to ride the offending motorcycle.

Taking into all these circumstances and the fact that the claimant was a pillion rider, this Court considers it appropriate to award a global NC: 2023:KHC-K:1137 compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- having regard to the injuries suffered by the claimant namely, the fracture of femur and tibia and the fracture of left palm.
12. In view of the above, the appeal is allowed in part and the impugned Judgment and award is set aside.

The appellant/claimant is entitled to global compensation of Rs.1,00,000/-, which shall be paid by the insurer along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization.
The compensation amount along with interest shall be deposited by the insurer before the Tribunal within a period of one month from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment and award.
Upon deposit, 50% of the enhanced compensation and interest shall be deposited in the name of the claimant in any nationalized Bank for a period of 3 years.
